subject: Request: temporary headcount buffer for quantized-batch kernel squad
messages:
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: HiringOps <hiringops@staffing.partner>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary headcount buffer for quantized-batch kernel squad

Team —

Quick ask: the quantized batch kernel work that the runtime team is doing needs an immediate, short-duration headcount buffer to hit the Q1 delivery committed to EdgeScale (see related HubSpot). Specifically we need either:

- Option A: 1 contract engineer (6 months) focused on kernel verification & integration (quantized fp16→8b path) OR
- Option B: 1 temporary FTE (6 months) converted to headcount buffer for the kernel squad.

Why now:
- EdgeScale committed to a pilot in Feb; the quantized path shows ~28% throughput improvement in our early tests but requires dedicated integration and regression testing to land safely.
- The work has high risk if we try to parallelize with current squad priorities; without a buffer we'll miss the pilot SLO.

Estimated budget and timeline:
- Budget: ~$55k–$70k fully loaded for 6 months depending on contractor vs temp-FTE.
- Target start: earliest feasible in Jan 2027 (candidate pipeline is already in motion).

Attachments: 2026-12-04-headcount-slate.xlsx (requested slot + delta), kernel-latency-analysis.pdf (benchmarks).

Ask: please approve a single temporary headcount buffer (6 months) or indicate an alternative cost owner. I can provide a candidate profile and quick interview plan. If approved, I'll loop procurement and HiringOps to push a requisition.

Thanks —
Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Platform Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: HiringOps <hiringops@staffing.partner>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headcount buffer for quantized-batch kernel squad

Hiro — thanks for the concise ask and the attachments. I skimmed the latency doc — good signal. A few quick notes:

1) Approvals: I can authorize up to $40k from my squad budget for a contractor. Anything above that needs either a cross-squad redistribution or an exec sign-off.
2) Duration & hire type: prefer contractor for speed (HiringOps can spin up). If this needs to be an FTE we should discuss comp band and approval window.
3) Risk: need Marcus to confirm there isn't a competing GPU-pool impact if we ramp up test infra.

Next steps: Marcus / Kimberly — can you weigh in on capacity and whether Finance has headroom? Jasmine — can you prep a short candidate profile template (2–3 bullets + sample interview exercise) so we can move quickly if approved?

If we get a greenlight today, I'll approve a contractor up to $40k and ask HiringOps to prep paperwork.

—Marissa
VP, Platform
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headcount buffer for quantized-batch kernel squad

+1 on the need — the throughput numbers look promising. A couple of practical constraints from infra:

- GPU pool: we have a scheduled maintenance window Jan 10–12 and limited burst capacity in the west region through mid-Jan unless we apply an emergency allocation. That may push the pilot into late Feb if we don't get burst capacity or an external contract.
- Impact: pulling an extra kernel engineer onto our shared build/release lane will add ~1.5 days/week of friction for the edge-serving squad; we should quantify that tradeoff.

Suggestion: leverage an external burst agreement (EdgeScale) for Jan testing + contractor for the integration work. EdgeScale can provision short-term capacity quickly (Satish at EdgeScale has been responsive). I've added the project plan link: https://docs.redwood.com/drive/quantized-kernel-capacity-plan-2026.

Jasmine — can you slot the interview exercise into next-week calendars if Marissa greenlights the contractor?

-Marcus
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: HiringOps <hiringops@staffing.partner>, EdgeScale Procurement <procurement@edgescale.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headcount buffer for quantized-batch kernel squad

Following up and confirming approvals:

On Mon, Dec 6, 2026 at 09:10 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hiro — thanks for the concise ask and the attachments. I skimmed the latency doc — good signal. A few quick notes:
>
> 1) Approvals: I can authorize up to $40k from my squad budget for a contractor. Anything above that needs either a cross-squad redistribution or an exec sign-off.
>
> Next steps: Marcus / Kimberly — can you weigh in on capacity and whether Finance has headroom? Jasmine — can you prep a short candidate profile template (2–3 bullets + sample interview exercise) so we can move quickly if approved?

After reviewing the numbers and the pilot schedule, I will provisionally approve:

- One temporary headcount buffer (contractor) for up to $60,000 total for 6 months, contingent on:
  * Procurement confirming EdgeScale burst availability for Jan testing, and
  * HiringOps confirming contractor onboarding can complete by Jan 12.

Procurement (EdgeScale) — can you confirm burst capability and send a short ELA/statement of work? Satish, if you can reply to procurement@redwood.com with availability that will help lock dates.

If both conditions are met, Marissa: please proceed with the contractor up to $60k and HiringOps — open the req and prioritize interviews. Marcus: please flag any infra fallout in the shared lane.

-Kimberly Park
Director, Finance & Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
